messages:
maria: Quick summary — ran FP8-KV vs INT8-KV on opt-6.7b (production config) against the short-chat sim (avg prompt 35 tokens). Memory: FP8 ~28% reduction, INT8 ~22%. P50 latencies look fine, but P99 cold-start spikes with FP8 (220ms -> 410ms). Suspect extra dequant work on cold path.

kevin: can you paste the exact bench command + outputs? also which kernel build?

maria: yes — command and tail of stdout:
```bash
./kv_bench --model opt-6.7b --quant fp8 --kv-only --batch 1 --prefill-stride 1 --runs 1000
```
perf slice:
```
mem_used_mb: 5120 -> 3700 (fp8)
p50: 45ms -> 48ms
p95: 120ms -> 140ms
p99: 220ms -> 410ms  # cold-start spike on some traces
```

maria: build is runtime-v2.4.1 + kernel-select opt-6.7b-optimized. These are non-AWQ FP8 paths.

jing: :thinking_face: hypothesis: FP8 dequant path is deferred until first KV read, so cold prefill triggers extra copy+dequant. INT8 path maybe does eager dequant during load. Can you check `--kv-dequant-on-prefill` toggle?

maria: good call — I toggled it. With `--kv-dequant-on-prefill=true` p99 drops to ~240ms (still slightly higher than INT8) and memory unchanged. So most of the spike is the lazy dequant.

sam: interesting. did you try AWQ/GPTQ variants? they sometimes avoid runtime dequant by storing already quantized-friendly layouts.

maria: not yet. I ran a quick AWQ shadow run earlier and saw similar mem gains but AWQ p99 better: ~260ms cold. will re-run properly.

kevin: can you upload the full trace and queue a shadow with prefill stride 2 + `--kv-dequant-on-prefill=true`? also include a run with `--prefill-mode=partial` to simulate streamed short prompts.

maria: uploaded traces: https://internal.redwood/bench/traces/2734567890/fp8-trace.log (permissions open to eng-ml). queued the two jobs.

benchbot: Job queued: 2734567901 (fp8, prefill-stride=2, kv-dequant-on-prefill=true), Job queued: 2734567920 (fp8, prefill-mode=partial). Estimated completion ~25m. :gear:

jing: once bench finishes, run diff on token-level latency distribution and check KV copy counts (we log dequant ops as DQ_OP). If DQ_OP > 0 on first token, that matches lazy dequant.

sam: also add an AWQ job for comparison and a tiny eval using short-chat-1k to catch quality delta from FP8 on short prompts. small losses could be amplified for very short context.

maria: adding AWQ job now and eval set short-chat-1k. queued. thanks all. :thumbsup:

kevin: if AWQ holds p99 and mem gains are close, we can consider FP8 for dedicated pools with a dequant-on-prefill default. Need notes for runtime change and perf toggle in rollout.

maria: noted — will draft a short ops doc with recommended defaults and a canary plan if AWQ/FP8 make it past regression gates.

benchbot: Job complete: 2734567901 — p99 245ms, mem 3720mb. Job complete: 2734567920 — p99 395ms, mem 3718mb. AWQ job complete: 2734567930 — p99 265ms, mem 3690mb. Artifacts: https://internal.redwood/bench/results/2734567890.zip

maria: preliminary takeaway: lazy dequant explains the large cold tail. `--kv-dequant-on-prefill` fixes most of the spike (FP8 p99 ~245ms). AWQ is promising (p99 265ms) and similar mem. Next: run 24h shadow on production traffic with dequant-on-prefill and AWQ compare.

jing: great. also add kernel-level counters to ensure we don't regress steady-state throughput with dequant prefill.

sam: I'll handle the AWQ follow-up and quality evals.

maria: thanks — I'll open a short PR to default `kv-dequant-on-prefill=true` behind a runtime flag + rollout notes. Follow-up in this thread once shadow results in. :eyes:
